_comment: PARENT workflow snippet. Replace the childJob's downstream extraction with this. Task ids are illustrative hex ids (adjust to fit your existing workflow's id scheme).

a1a1.name: childJob
a1a1.description: Runs a child job inside a workflow.

b2b2.name: query
b2b2.summary: Extract taskStatus for every child (correct: wildcard projection)
b2b2.description: Projects the taskStatus field across every loop iteration in job_details in a single call. This is the fix for issue #1: query:'loop' alone returns the FULL flat-spread object per child (status, childJobLoopIndex, every child job variable including taskStatus) -- it does NOT hand you a pre-filtered list of just taskStatus values. A literal query of 'loop' followed by treating the result as if it already were '[taskStatus, taskStatus, ...]', or a second query with query:'taskStatus' run against that array, will resolve to null/undefined every time, because an array has no top-level 'taskStatus' key -- only its elements do. Use the '[**]' wildcard to reach into every element of the array and pull the one field you want.

c3c3.name: query
c3c3.summary: Extract full loop array for correlation by childJobLoopIndex
c3c3.description: Keep the FULL per-child objects (not just taskStatus) if downstream logic needs to match a status back to a specific device. loopType:'parallel' does not guarantee the array preserves data_array input order -- each element's 'childJobLoopIndex' field exists specifically so you can correlate a result back to its original input position/device. Fix for issue #2: never assume returnArray[i] corresponds to devices[i] when loopType is 'parallel'; always match on childJobLoopIndex (or a natural key like deviceName that you also pass into the child) instead of raw array position.

d4d4.name: evaluation
d4d4.summary: Guard: did every child report a status?
d4d4.description: Defensive check before trusting childTaskStatuses downstream. contains is the universal 'does X contain Y' operator -- on a string operand it does regex matching, on an array/object operand it can be used to test membership/key presence. Wire this against the projected array to catch the case where the CHILD workflow itself failed to set taskStatus on some completion path (issue #3) rather than a parent-side query bug. If this evaluation fails, do not trust downstream taskStatus checks -- go inspect the specific child job (childJobLoopIndex from c3c3's output) whose element is missing the key.

d4d4._comment: wire success -> continue normal flow, failure -> your error/investigation branch
